topic: Newton’s Laws of Motion: Inertia and Acceleration
key_concepts: Inertia is the tendency of an object to resist changes in motion.
Newton’s first law is the law of inertia.
An object at rest remains at rest unless acted on by an unbalanced force.
Inertia depends on mass, not speed.
An unbalanced force changes an object’s speed or motion.
Newton’s first law applies to both moving and stationary objects.
Net force of zero does not mean inertia is zero.
Acceleration increases when greater force is applied.
Adding mass reduces acceleration for a given force.
Newton’s second law relates force, mass, and acceleration as F=ma.
Force is measured in newtons, mass in kilograms, and acceleration in m/s².
